RagShortTexts: The Dampierre dynasty governed prosperous Flemish weaving cities, balancing royal.

Variants.Content: The House of Dampierre commanded the textile heartland of Flanders under Guy of Dampierre. Caught between independent cloth-guild communes like Bruges and Ghent and long succession wars against the Avesnes, the dynasty relied on English wool while resisting encroaching Capetian suzerainty from Paris.
A Flemish count yields vast mercantile wealth, yet rules on the knife-edge of burgher revolts and ferocious urban pike militias.
The weavers of Ghent pay countal duties solely to preserve ancient charters. Disrupt the English fleece convoys, and dockworkers will shut the rivergates.
